c.tagline: Canada's Festival City - West Edmonton Mall, a sprawling river valley, and the gateway to the north.

taxi.color: varied (Yellow Cab, Co-op Taxi, Capital Taxi)
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around C$3.60 plus per-km and per-minute charges. App-based Uber and Lyft both operate citywide and are often cheaper than a hailed cab.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance across Canada; 811 (Health Link) is Alberta's non-emergency health line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Downtown / Ice District: Rogers Place Ice District Edmonton downtown skyline

avoid.reason: Parts of the downtown core, Chinatown, and LRT stations can feel sketchy late at night due to visible social disorder — stay alert after dark.

hood_desc: Edmonton's revitalized core, anchored by the Ice District and Rogers Place arena, with high-rise hotels, restaurants, the Art Gallery of Alberta and the Capital and Valley LRT lines meeting here; the most walkable, transit-connected base.

The city's historic entertainment quarter south of the North Saskatchewan River, centered on Whyte Avenue with its pubs, live-music venues, cafes, vintage shops and the summer Fringe Theatre Festival; best for nightlife and a youthful, walkable scene.

The sprawling west-side district built around West Edmonton Mall - for decades North America's largest mall, with an indoor water park, rides and hundreds of shops - plus big-box retail and hotel-strip lodging; a car helps here.

A creative strip just west of downtown along 124 Street, lined with art galleries, indie boutiques, coffee roasters and some of the city's best restaurants; suits travelers who want an arty, local, walkable pocket.

A leafy, upscale older residential neighborhood on the river-valley bluffs west of downtown, home to Government House and steps from the river-valley trail network; quiet, green and scenic - good for a calm base.
lodging: Days Inn by Wyndham Edmonton Downtown

water.note: Tap water is safe and good quality.

transit.hours: LRT and most buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around 1:00 AM, with reduced late-night frequency and limited overnight service.
transit.pay: Tap the reloadable Arc smart card on LRT platform validators and bus readers, or pay a cash single fare on board buses; an adult fare is C$2.75 and covers 90 minutes of transfers, with Arc automatically capping daily and monthly spend once you've ridden enough.

bus: Red Arrow / Ebus / FlixBus (intercity to Calgary, Red Deer, Fort McMurray)
train: VIA Rail Edmonton (the Canadian, Toronto-Vancouver, ~3x weekly)

transit.m: ETS Route 747 to Century Park LRT, then Capital Line downtown (~60 min)
Airport shuttle / hotel shuttles to select downtown and west-end hotels

food.name: Green onion cake
food.desc: Crisp, chewy scallion pancake invented in Edmonton in the 1970s and now the city's unofficial dish at every festival and market.

places.name: Green Onion Cake Man
places.note: Siu To created the dish here; still the version everyone else is judged against.

places.name: Old Strathcona Farmers Market
places.note: Weekend market stalls fry them to order alongside other local snacks.

places.name: City Market Downtown
places.note: Summer street market where green onion cake vendors set up most weeks.

food.name: Ukrainian perogies
food.desc: Potato-and-cheddar dumplings boiled then pan-fried with onion and bacon, sour cream on the side; Edmonton has a deep Ukrainian community.

places.name: Uncle Ed's Ukrainian Restaurant
places.note: Long-standing family restaurant making perogies fresh daily.

places.name: Shumka Ukrainian Foods
places.note: Deli-style shop selling perogies and cabbage rolls by the dozen to take home.

places.name: Taste of Ukraine
places.note: Popular sit-down Ukrainian kitchen just east of the city.

food.name: Alberta beef steak
food.desc: Grain-finished Alberta beef, usually a ribeye or striploin, from a province with more cattle than people.

places.name: Hardware Grill
places.note: Downtown institution in a heritage building, strong on Alberta beef and game.

places.name: Rge Rd
places.note: Farm-to-table kitchen sourcing whole animals from Alberta ranches.

places.name: Ruth's Chris Steak House
places.note: Reliable big-steak option in the core when you want a classic steakhouse.

food.name: Donair
food.desc: Canadian riff on the doner: spiced beef loaf shaved off the spit into a warm pita with tomato, onion and sweet condensed-milk garlic sauce.

places.name: Marco's Famous
places.note: Regularly named in local best-donair lists; the safe first stop.

places.name: Swiss Donair
places.note: Veteran shop with a devoted following for its sauce.

places.name: Top Donair
places.note: Late-night favourite in a city with well over a hundred donair shops.

food.name: Kubasa and cabbage rolls
food.desc: Garlicky Ukrainian smoked sausage with holubtsi, rice-stuffed cabbage rolls baked in tomato sauce; prairie holiday food eaten year round.

places.name: Widynowski's Sausage House
places.note: Old-school sausage maker locals buy kubasa from by the ring.

places.name: Uncle Ed's Ukrainian Restaurant
places.note: Full Ukrainian platters with sausage, holubtsi and perogies together.

places.name: Shumka Ukrainian Foods
places.note: Frozen and ready-made cabbage rolls made in-house.

food.name: Saskatoon berry pie
food.desc: Prairie berry, closer to an almond-scented blueberry, baked into pies and tarts through the short northern summer.

places.name: Old Strathcona Farmers Market
places.note: Bakers sell saskatoon pies and jams when the berries come in.

places.name: City Market Downtown
places.note: Seasonal stalls with prairie-berry baking and preserves.

places.name: Sunterra Market
places.note: Alberta grocer that carries saskatoon pies and desserts outside market season.

food.name: Alberta craft beer
food.desc: Edmonton's brewery scene runs from prairie-grain lagers to barrel-aged sours, much of it made within a few kilometres of downtown.

places.name: Alley Kat Brewing
places.note: Alberta's oldest surviving craft brewery, with a taproom and growler fills.

places.name: Blind Enthusiasm Brewing
places.note: Known for farmhouse and barrel-aged beers in a converted neighbourhood space.

places.name: Situation Brewing
places.note: Brewpub on Whyte Avenue pouring its own beer with full food service.

food.name: Caesar
food.desc: Canada's own cocktail: vodka with clamato, hot sauce and Worcestershire on a salted rim, garnished to increasingly ridiculous lengths.

places.name: The Next Act
places.note: Whyte Avenue pub that pours a proper loaded Caesar with the burgers.

places.name: Denizen Hall
places.note: Big downtown hall known for oversized brunch Caesars.

places.name: Craft Beer Market
places.note: Weekend brunch spot with a build-your-own Caesar list.

landmarks: West Edmonton Mall
One of the world's largest shopping and entertainment complexes, complete with an indoor water park and amusement park, making it a bucket-list oddity.
Muttart Conservatory
Four striking glass pyramids rising from the river valley house distinct climate zones and lush plant collections, forming an unmistakable city icon.
Alberta Legislature Building
This grand Edwardian-style domed building overlooking the river valley is Alberta's seat of government and one of Edmonton's most photographed landmarks.
High Level Bridge
This dramatic steel trestle bridge spans the North Saskatchewan River and is famous for its seasonal waterfall display down its center.
Fort Edmonton Park
North America's largest living history museum recreates four eras of Edmonton's past across a sprawling riverside site, perfect for immersive photos.
North Saskatchewan River Valley
The longest stretch of connected urban parkland in North America winds through the city, offering endless scenic river and skyline views.
Royal Alberta Museum
Western Canada's largest museum showcases Alberta's natural and human history in a striking modern building near the legislature grounds.
TELUS World of Science Edmonton
Its iconic angular, futuristic architecture and giant planetarium dome make this science centre a distinctive fixture of the city's skyline.
Rogers Place / Ice District
The sleek, ultramodern home of the Edmonton Oilers anchors the vibrant Ice District, a glowing hub of downtown nightlife and architecture.
Commonwealth Stadium
Canada's largest outdoor stadium has hosted Commonwealth Games and world championships, and remains a striking landmark on the river valley's edge.

train.note: No international trains. VIA Rail's transcontinental Canadian calls at Edmonton two or three times a week on its Toronto-Vancouver run, reaching Jasper in about 5 hours and Vancouver in a further 17 - it is a scenic journey rather than a practical way to travel, and it frequently runs late behind freight traffic. The station is well north of downtown. Book sleeper berths months ahead for summer.

bus.note: No international coaches. Red Arrow (https://www.redarrow.ca/), Ebus (https://myebus.ca/) and FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.ca/) run to Calgary in about 3h30 and Jasper, with Rider Express (https://riderexpress.ca/) heading east toward Saskatoon and Winnipeg. There is no single central bus terminal - check your operator's pickup point.

ferry.note: Edmonton is deep inland on the prairies beside the North Saskatchewan River, which carries no scheduled service, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Elk Island National Park
half.blurb: Fenced prairie park protecting free-roaming bison herds, with hiking trails and lakes just east of the city.

half.name: Drumheller (Royal Tyrrell Museum)
half.blurb: Badlands town of hoodoos and dinosaur fossil beds, home to one of the world's leading paleontology museums.

full.name: Jasper National Park
full.blurb: Rocky Mountain wilderness park with turquoise lakes, glaciers, and the Icefields Parkway, reached via a long scenic drive.
